title: The Orbit of Station Meridian
premise: Cyrus Underhill smuggles memories through the contested orbits of Station Meridian, where a fragile truce between the colonial Fleet and the corporate Combine holds two fleets apart. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream — a memory no one planted, broadcasting from the station's sealed core — Cyrus is hired to trace its origin and discovers it is the recorded consciousness of Meridian's founder, kept alive as leverage by both sides. As the truce clock runs down, she must keep alive the lie that the founder still speaks, brokering peace between fleets who each believe they alone hold her voice. In the end, Cyrus releases the founder's memory to every mind on the station at once, ending the lie and forcing both fleets to negotiate in the open — at the cost of her cargo, her cover, and the quiet life she built.
about_author: Lena Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard supply vessels before turning to fiction. She writes about people who live in the gaps between jurisdictions, where law thins out and conscience has to do the work.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Cyrus runs a routine memory-smuggling job past orbital customs, establishing her methods, her contacts, and the twenty-year truce that keeps her trade possible. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she's good at surviving and bad at living.

chapters.title: The Dream That Belongs to Everyone
chapters.summary: Children across the colony wake reciting the same dream: a woman drowning in light inside a metal room. Cyrus is approached by a Fleet officer, Ade Osei, who knows her real name and offers payment she can't refuse. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: unease — the dream feels familiar to her too.

chapters.title: Customs House Ghosts
chapters.summary: Cyrus traces the dream's signal through black-market relays while dodging Combine surveillance. She learns the broadcast originates from the station's sealed core, off-limits since the founding war. POV: Cyrus, with a brief interlude from a child dreamer. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: The Founder's Voice
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Ade breach the core and find the founder, Ilsa Meridian, preserved as a conscious recording — held hostage by both fleets as proof of legitimacy. Each side believes it alone controls her voice. POV: alternating Cyrus and Ade. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at what survival has cost.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Ade reveals the truce expires in thirty days; both fleets plan to seize the core and claim the founder. He asks Cyrus to help maintain the fiction that Ilsa speaks for the Fleet. POV: Ade. Emotional beat: duty versus growing love for Cyrus and doubt about his own side.

chapters.title: What the Combine Bought
chapters.summary: A Combine broker offers Cyrus citizenship and immunity if she delivers Ilsa's memory archive. Torn, she takes the meeting and secretly copies everything instead. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: temptation and self-loathing; she realizes she's become the thing she smuggles — a lie with a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: The children's dream intensifies, spreading to adults; riots spark at the docks. Both fleets mobilize. Cyrus and Ade grow closer while building a fake 'new message' from Ilsa to buy time. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: intimacy under countdown pressure, tenderness sharpened by dread.

chapters.title: The Broken Signal
chapters.summary: The Combine exposes the forgery; Ade is arrested for treason, and Cyrus's smuggling network is burned. Alone, she confronts Ilsa directly and learns the founder wants to be released, not owned. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: rock bottom — everything lost except the truth.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Cyrus storms the core during the fleet standoff and releases Ilsa's full memory into every mind on Meridian at once. The fleets' soldiers, suddenly sharing one consciousness's grief, lower their weapons. POV: Cyrus, dissolving briefly into collective memory. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, dissolution, and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Orbit We Choose
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, freed from the lie, Fleet and Combine delegates negotiate openly while the children's dream fades into ordinary sleep. Cyrus, stripped of her trade but not her name, chooses to stay — with Ade, with the station, with the truth. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; survival finally worth its price.
